## Dataset: Aerosol Data Weissfluhjoch

Aerosol properties were measured between February 8 and March 31 2019  at the measurement site Weissfluhjoch &#40;LON: 9.806475, LAT: 46.832964&#41;. Optical and aerodynamic particle counters, as well as a scanning mobility particle size spectrometer and an ice nuclei counter were deployed to report particle concentrations and size distributions in fine &#40;10-1000 nm&#41; and coarse mode &#40;- 1000 nm&#41;, cloud condensation nuclei concentrations &#40;CCNCs&#41;, and ice nuclei particle concentrations &#40;ICNCs&#41;. The ambient particles were transported via a heated inlet to be distributed to the particle detecting devices inside the setup room. <br>Optical Particle Counter &#40;OPC&#41;: Light scattering of a diode laser beam caused by travelling particles is used in the both, the OPC-N3 &#40;0.41 - 38.5 &amp;956;m&#41; and GT-526S &#40;0.3 – 5 &amp;956;m&#41;, to determine their size and number concentration. For the OPC-N3, particle size spectra and concentration data are used afterwards to calculate PM&amp;8321;, PM&amp;8322;,&amp;8325; and PM&amp;8321;&amp;8320; &#40;assumptions: particle density: 1.65 g cm&amp;713;&amp;179;, refractive index: 1.5+i0&#41;. <br>Aerodynamic Particle Sizer &#40;APS&#41;: The APS &#40;3321, TSI Inc.&#41; measured the particle size distribution for aerodynamic diameters between 0.5 &amp;956;m and &#126;20 &amp;956;m by the particle’s time-of-flight and light-scattering intensity &#40;assumptions: particle density 1 g cm&amp;713;&amp;179;&#41;. <br>Scanning Mobility Particle Size Spectrometer &#40;SMPS&#41;: Particle number concentrations in a size range between 12 and 460 nm &#40;electrical mobility diameter&#41; were measured at Davos Wolfgang, using a Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer Spectrometer &#40;SMPS 3938, TSI Inc.&#41;. The classifier &#40;3082, TSI Inc.&#41; was equipped with a neutralizer &#40;3088, TSI Inc.&#41; and a differential mobility analyzer working with negative polarity &#40;3081, TSI Inc.&#41;. The size selected particles were counted by a water-based condensation particle counter &#40;3787 TSI Inc.&#41;. The TSI AIM software was used to provide particle size distributions by applying multiple charge and diffusion loss corrections &#40;assumptions: particle density 1 g cm&amp;713;&amp;179;&#41;. <br>Coriolis &amp;956; and LINDA: A microbial air sampler &#40;Coriolis &amp;956;, bertin Instruments&#41; was used to collect airborne particles for investigating their ice nucleating ability with a droplet freezing device. Particles larger than 0.5 &amp;956;m were drawn with an air flow rate of up to 300 l min&amp;8254;&amp;185; into the cone and centrifuged into the wall of the cone due to the forming vortex. The liquid sample was transferred into the LED based Ice Nucleation Detection Apparatus &#40;LINDA, University of Basel&#41; to study heterogeneous ice formation &#40;immersion freezing mode&#41; of ambient airborne particles.

[View this dataset in the data catalogue](https://opendata.swiss/de/dataset/aerosol-data-weissfluhjoch)

## Load packages

This template targets tidyverse (2.x) and skimr (2.x) with R 4.1 or newer for the native `|>` pipe; package versions are not pinned. Install missing packages once with `install.packages(c("tidyverse", "skimr"))`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

USER_AGENT <- "OpendataSwiss-StarterCode-R/1.0"
HTTP_TIMEOUT <- 30

get_dataset <- function(url, delim = NULL, drop_empty_unnamed = TRUE, ...) {
  if (grepl("^https?://", url)) {
    local_file <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(local_file), add = TRUE)
    old_options <- options(timeout = HTTP_TIMEOUT)
    on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
    status <- download.file(url, local_file, method = "libcurl", mode = "wb",
                            quiet = TRUE, headers = c("User-Agent" = USER_AGENT))
    if (status != 0) stop("Resource download failed")
    url <- local_file
  }
  data <- read_delim(url, delim = delim, show_col_types = FALSE, ...)
  stop_for_problems(data)
  if (drop_empty_unnamed && nrow(data) > 0) {
    # Blank CSV headers (often from trailing separators) become "...n".
    unnamed <- grepl("^\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", names(data))
    empty_unnamed <- unnamed & map_lgl(data, ~ all(is.na(.x)))
    if (any(empty_unnamed)) {
      message("Removed empty unnamed columns: ", paste(names(data)[empty_unnamed], collapse = ", "))
      data <- data[, !empty_unnamed, drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  data
}
```

## Load data

Selected resource: **3cc70513-0e6b-4873-911a-97a1f42f9a0c** (CSV). This notebook loads only this resource.

For CSV, the delimiter and column types are guessed. Check the preview and metadata; set `delim`, `col_types`, `na`, or `locale` in `get_dataset(...)` when needed (for example, read identifiers with leading zeros as character columns). Parsing problems stop the import so they can be addressed.

Fully empty columns named `...n` are removed on import. Named empty columns and unnamed columns containing values are kept. Use `drop_empty_unnamed = FALSE` to retain every column, including intentionally named `...n` fields.


## Missing values

```{r missing-values}
missing <- tibble(
  column = names(df),
  missing = map_int(df, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  missing_pct = map_dbl(df, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))
missing

# Show up to 20 columns with missing values; percentages use all rows.
missing_plot <- missing |> filter(missing > 0) |> slice_head(n = 20)
if (nrow(missing_plot) > 0) {
  ggplot(missing_plot, aes(x = missing_pct, y = reorder(column, missing_pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "Missing values (%)", y = NULL, title = "Missingness by column")
} else {
  message("No missing values to plot (or the dataset has no rows).")
}
```

## Summary and distributions

`skim()` reports completeness and type-specific summaries. Inspect units before interpreting numeric codes as measurements.

```{r histograms}
# Plot up to four numeric columns, excluding non-finite values only from plots.
numeric_names <- names(select(df, where(is.numeric))) |> head(4)
for (column in numeric_names) {
  values <- df[[column]]
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  if (length(values) > 0) {
    plot <- ggplot(tibble(value = values), aes(x = value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
      labs(title = column, x = column, y = "Count")
    print(plot)
  }
}
```

```{r category-counts}
# Top 10 values for up to three categorical columns, including missing values.
categorical_names <- df |>
  select(where(~ is.character(.x) || is.factor(.x) || is.logical(.x))) |>
  names() |>
  head(3)
for (column in categorical_names) {
  cat(column, "\n")
  df |> count(.data[[column]], sort = TRUE) |> head(10) |> print()
}
```
